body:
Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-24: several logins on one server are allowed, so a list (and an
item) can be held by more than one account on this phone. Today `lists.id` and `items.id` are the
server ids, so two accounts sharing a list collide on the primary key (T-298 item 2 only narrowed the
window). Step "B1b" of the multi-account design (T-289), ahead of B2 (T-292).

## Model (schema 10)

* Every row gets a phone-local surrogate primary key: `lists.localId`, `items.localId` (UUIDs). The
  server id stays as `lists.id` / `items.id` (rename to `serverId` only if it keeps the diff readable;
  the wire name is unchanged either way).
* `items.listLocalId` references `lists.localId`; `items.accountId` is denormalised so per-account
  item queries need no join (keep it in step with the list's account; a check in the DAO tests).
* Unique indices: `lists(accountId, id)`, `items(accountId, id)`; index `items(listLocalId)`.
* Screens, routes, last-opened list, notifications and deep links keep passing ONE id: the local one.
  `ListsRepo`/`ItemsRepo` take local ids; the sync engine is the only place that maps server ids to
  rows, per account (`getByServerId(accountId, id)`), and the push side sends the server id.
* The migration keeps every existing row, mints local ids, rewrites `items.listLocalId` from the
  old `listId`, and fills `items.accountId` from the list. Last-opened list id in the secret store
  is a server id today: translate it (the single account's row) or drop it. Test the migration on a
  schema-9 database with two lists and items, and on the stub lists T-298 added.
* `PendingInvite`, `CollaboratorChange` and the registry screen keep working by local id.

## Rules

* A pull merges a DTO into the row of (syncing account, server id), creating it under that account
  when absent. Two accounts that share a list therefore hold two rows, each with its own clocks,
  dirty flags and quarantine; that is intended, the server reconciles them.
* Removing an account removes only its rows; nothing of another account is touched, and no cursor
  reset is needed any more (T-298 item 2's reset goes).
* `updated_by` stays the device id.

## Out of scope

No UI change; the CurrentAccount shim stays until B2. No wire change; `docs/wire-contract.md` is
untouched. android/README.md describes the local id in one paragraph.
title: Android: lists and items keyed by a phone-local id, unique per account and server id (B1b)
